ashby:9fin:f585cf19-142f-4eea-8dc2-d2c31.summary:
9fin is the AI platform powering global debt markets — the world’s largest asset class at over $145 trillion.

Debt markets are vast, global, and mission-critical, yet still run on fragmented data, PDFs, and manual workflows. 9fin replaces this broken infrastructure with a single platform that centralises proprietary credit data, deep analysis, and high-value workflows across global markets.

Today, 9fin powers teams at 300+ blue-chip institutions worldwide, including global banks, asset managers, private equity firms, law firms, and advisors. The business is scaling at exceptional speed, with rapid expansion in the US and best-in-class retention driven by deep workflow adoption.

sections.title: About 9fin
paras: We’re at a defining inflection point. With proven product-market fit and strong, global market pull, 9fin is accelerating toward becoming the category-defining platform for debt markets worldwide.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: We’re looking for a Head of Strategic Accounts, US to lead the top tier of our commercial organization — the largest, most complex accounts driving 9fin’s next phase of growth. Strategics is our top segment: a targeted book of our largest ARR accounts across the global banks, top-tier law firms, multi-strategy hedge funds, asset managers, and private equity firms who set the standard for how credit intelligence is bought and used.

You’ll build and lead a team of ~5–6 senior relationship managers in New York, each owning a small portfolio of strategic accounts in a hybrid Account Management and Enterprise Sales role. You’ll partner closely with our Head of Strategic Accounts, EMEA to run a globally coordinated segment and work with senior Customer Success partners at the account level.

This is a builder role for a leader who has personally carried a large number, sold enterprise-scale deals into financial services, and knows how to raise the bar on rigor, presence, and multi-year deal execution.

sections.title: What you’ll work on
paras: Every day is different, but here’s an example of the kind of things you’ll work on:
bullets: Lead the US Strategics team to consistent, forecastable delivery quarter over quarter across a book of $13M+ ARR accounts.
Coach and manage a team of ~5–6 Strategic Account Managers covering our most important banks, asset managers, hedge funds, private equity firms, and law firms in the US.
Drive multi-year deal execution, lock in early renewals, and structure enterprise agreements that grow durably over time.
Coach the team through complex commercial motions — MSAs, procurement, legal review, and executive alignment at the MD, Partner, PM, Head of Desk, and C-suite level.
Run weekly segment reviews focused on deals moved, deals at risk, pipeline health, and account-level path-to-close plans.
Set the operating cadence for the segment. Enforce our 3-day office minimum, and drive territory planning, account mapping, and a shared deal methodology across the team.
Partner with the EMEA Head of Strategic Accounts to build geographic reciprocity, with US AMs backing up EMEA coverage on global accounts, and vice versa.
Work in a “two-in-the-box” model with senior CSMs (product and usage) and Sales Engineering (pre-sales), and partner across Enablement, Rev Ops, Marketing, and Product to remove barriers to growth.

sections.title: About You
bullets: Have 12+ years of enterprise B2B sales experience, including 4+ years leading strategic or enterprise sales teams selling into financial services (banks, asset managers, hedge funds, PE firms), law firms, or a mix.

Have personally carried and consistently exceeded a large individual quota on multi-million-dollar strategic accounts, and can point to specific accounts you’ve grown from $X to $Y and explain exactly how.
Bring a consultative approach to selling and want to become a strategic partner to our clients

Have deep familiarity with capital markets, credit, or the debt markets ecosystem across credit, leveraged finance, restructuring, distressed, and private credit — you can hold your own with a restructuring lawyer, a leveraged finance banker, or a credit PM.
Have led teams through multi-year deal execution and understand what it takes to secure meaningful year-over-year uplifts, early renewals, and complex enterprise agreements.
Can coach reps through complex procurement, MSA negotiation, legal review, and executive alignment at the MD, Partner, PM, Head of Desk, and C-suite level.
Bring C-suite presence and cross-organizational credibility. You show up sharp, prepared, and trusted by both your team and your customers.
Are a proactive coach, not a reactive manager. You share process, mentor your reps, and help them plan deals in advance rather than reacting to slipped forecasts.

ashby:c1:1521592b-6fb5-4105-b75f-6bb361c.summary:
C1.ai is the universal control plane that powers the agentic enterprise.

Every organization runs on hundreds of systems that need to answer the same basic question: who can do what, when, and why?

We're building something foundational: a horizontal control plane that lets both humans and AI agents plug in to navigate the AI-enabled enterprise, to understand who and what has access, and manage it safely as agents take on more of the work. SaaS apps, infrastructure, internal tools, AI agents…if it has a concept of 'who,' it should connect to us.

While we are still small in number, we move fast. If you want to help build this from the ground up, you'll have real ownership here.

sections.title: The Role
paras: This role is responsible for owning and evolving a core area of C1's Identity Governance platform. You'll partner closely with customers, Customer Success, and Engineering to deliver new capabilities, improve existing workflows, and ensure our platform continues to solve mission-critical identity challenges for enterprise customers. This is an execution-focused product role where strong product judgment, deep domain expertise, and customer empathy matter as much as product strategy.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Own a core area of C1's Identity Governance & Administration (IGA) platform, driving product strategy, roadmap execution, and customer outcomes for a mature, enterprise-scale product surface.
Partner closely with Engineering, Customer Success, Support, and Sales to prioritize customer needs, resolve escalations, and continuously improve product quality, reliability, and usability.
Translate customer feedback, usage data, and market insights into well-defined product investments that balance customer impact, technical complexity, and long-term platform strategy.
Make thoughtful prioritization decisions across feature development, technical debt, scalability, and operational improvements to maximize customer value.
Define clear product requirements and success metrics, ensuring engineering teams have the context needed to deliver high-quality solutions.
Work cross-functionally with Design, Engineering, Go-to-Market, and Customer Success to successfully launch new capabilities for existing products and drive customer adoption.
Monitor product health through customer feedback, adoption metrics, operational signals, and business outcomes, using data to inform future investment decisions.
Serve as the product expert for your domain, communicating roadmap priorities, tradeoffs, and strategic direction to internal stakeholders and customers.

sections.title: You'll likely have:
bullets: 5+ years of Product Management experience building and scaling enterprise SaaS products, preferably in cybersecurity, identity, or infrastructure software.
Deep domain expertise in Identity Governance & Administration (IGA), Identity and Access Management (IAM), privileged access, authentication, authorization, or adjacent security technologies.
Experience owning a mature product area, balancing customer requests, strategic investments, platform improvements, and operational excellence.
Strong product judgment and a demonstrated ability to prioritize competing customer needs, technical constraints, and business objectives.
Experience partnering closely with Customer Success and Engineering to solve real customer challenges and deliver measurable business outcomes.
A data-informed approach to product management, using qualitative customer insights and quantitative product metrics to guide decision-making.
A collaborative, ownership-oriented mindset with the ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence technical and non-technical stakeholders across Engineering, Design, Go-to-Market, Customer Success, and executive leadership.

ashby:choco:0adad417-869f-4342-8058-51be.summary:
Join Choco, where we build and own solutions that reshape a broken food system.

The global food supply chain is inefficient by design. Waste is high, margins are thin, and most distributor order processes are done over the phone, tracked across broad spreadsheets, and based on intuition rather than strong data.

At Choco, we’re changing that. We build software used daily by food distributors and their customers to run their business. It automates orders, reduces errors, and helps operations run faster and more reliably. Because it’s embedded in daily operations, our SaaS platform has immediate, real-world impact, on efficiency, margins, and how businesses run day to day.

sections.title: Mission
paras: As a Solutions Engineer, you will deliver fast, reliable, API-driven integrations for mid-market customers by translating business workflows into scalable, repeatable technical solutions. You will partner closely with Sales and Customer Success to deliver best-in-class integration experiences that drive adoption and long-term success. This role is primarily customer-facing, with a strong focus on solution design and customer outcomes rather than traditional software development. You'll build integrations primarily with low-code tools, using light scripting where needed.

sections.title: What You’ll Do
bullets: Design, build, and deliver integrations between Choco and customer systems using low-code tools (e.g. n8n and Tray.ai ).
Own integration projects end-to-end from discovery to go-live and ongoing improvement.
Partner with Account Executives in pre-sales by leading technical discovery, proofs of concept, and integration scoping.
Troubleshoot and maintain integrations to ensure reliability and performance, and document integration designs for clean handoffs to Customer Success.
Collaborate closely with Customer Success, Implementation, and Product teams, sharing customer feedback to help shape the product roadmap.
Share best practices and contribute to scaling integration delivery globally.

sections.title: What You Bring
bullets: 1+ years of experience in solutions engineering, IT/ERP consulting, or systems integration.
Bachelor’s degree in business, technology, or a related field.
Experience with low-code or automation tools such as n8n, Zapier, and Tray.ai .
Experience delivering API integrations across multiple customer environments, from discovery and design through launch and ongoing support.
Basic programming knowledge (e.g. JavaScript or Python) and working knowledge of REST APIs, JSON/XML, webhooks, authentication (OAuth, API keys), and data mapping.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a collaborative, solution-focused mindset.
Excellent communicator with the ability to make complex ideas clear and simple.
This position requires in-office attendance 3 days per week (T/W/Th) in our Chicago office.

sections.title: Nice to Have

Background in food distribution, supply chain, or B2B SaaS.

ashby:cloaked:3337d6d2-9b42-48e8-a5fe-34.summary:
Cloaked is a privacy startup dedicated to rebuilding consumer trust in how personal data is used. Nearly a million paying members use Cloaked to take back control of their data, their identity, and who can reach them. That covers masked emails, phone numbers, and payment cards, data removal from broker sites, and an AI voice agent that screens calls before they ring through.

We've protected tens of millions of identities, screened hundreds of millions of calls, and removed billions of records from data brokers. Backed by a $375M Series B.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: We’re hiring a Senior Product Marketing Manager, Lifecycle & Consumer Education to own the customer after the signup. Cloaked is good at acquiring customers and shipping features. This role makes sure the people we acquire understand what they bought, use it, stay, and buy more. You’ll own every owned communication surface (email, push, SMS, in-app, and the help and support content layer with CX) with one job: grow lifetime value by driving retention, feature adoption, and expansion, and grow consumer trust in Cloaked while doing it. The role spans consumer and enterprise, and the outcomes are the same on both sides. If you’re a lifecycle marketer who thinks in customer moments rather than channels, come build with us!
This role is based in our New York office, in person three days a week.

sections.title: What will you do?
bullets: Own retention end to end: activation and onboarding, ongoing engagement, renewal, dunning and involuntary-churn recovery, save flows, and winback. Rebuild the programs that exist, build the ones that don’t, and run them on a documented experiment cadence.

Own upsell and expansion across every communication surface: monthly-to-annual conversion, plan tiers, add-ons, and family and multi-user plans. Find the moments where a customer is ready for more and build the programs that convert them, partnering with product on in-app surfaces and with the growth team on pricing and packaging tests.

Run consumer trust as a lifecycle program: transparency and “what we did for you” reporting, security and policy updates, proactive communication when something goes wrong (with CX and legal), and the standards that keep every message on brand and non-manipulative.

Build the same motion for enterprise customers: onboarding and seat activation, admin and end-user education, adoption reporting, renewal and expansion communication, and reference and advocacy programs, working with account owners.

Own the lifecycle stack end to end - Customer.io segmentation, journeys, templates, and QA; email and SMS deliverability; consent and preference management; and the lifecycle dashboard the team runs on. Supply customer stories and retention and trust proof points to PR and brand.

sections.title: What skills and experiences will help you?
bullets: 6–8 years in lifecycle, CRM, retention, or customer marketing at a consumer subscription or app business; prosumer or B2B customer-marketing experience alongside consumer is ideal.
Fluent in the data: comfortable in product analytics and SQL, builds your own cohorts and dashboards, and designs experiments with real control groups and sound denominators.

Strong writer and editor of customer-facing copy: clear, warm, direct, and on brand. You can explain a complex privacy feature to a non-technical customer in two sentences and know when to show rather than tell.
Product-minded: you understand activation and habit loops, can read a feature spec and map the adoption journey, and work with product and engineering on in-app surfaces, events, and triggers.
Systems operator: you’ve owned a marketing automation platform including deliverability, consent, and data integrations, and can scope the engineering work to make a journey possible.
Collaborative across functions: you work easily with CX, product, finance, and sales, and can run a program that touches four teams without owning any of them.
Fluent with AI tooling (Claude, ChatGPT) for drafting, variant generation, and analysis.
Bonus: a retention, adoption, or expansion program you built with a quantified lift against a holdout, or a lifecycle stack you rebuilt and left measurably healthier than you found it.

sections.title: What do we like?
bullets: Customer-obsessed, not channel-obsessed. Thinks in customer moments and outcomes first; email, push, and in-app are just the ways to get there.
Data-first and honest about it. Wants the holdout, reads the denominator, and says so when a program didn’t work.
Writes like a human. Keeps Cloaked’s warm, direct, non-fear-based voice even when the subject is scams, breaches, and renewals.
Systems builder. Enjoys making the plumbing work: events, segments, consent, deliverability. Leaves the stack better than they found it.
Comfortable on a small team. Owns outcomes that depend on CX, product, and sales without owning those teams.

sections.title: Short on time? TL;DR
bullets: You: Experienced PM who's shipped complex B2B products where real people, and something in the physical world, have to show up for the product to work. The messier the problem space, the more at home you'll feel here
Us: Team of ~60 including a growing team of 14 engineers, lab volume 6x’d in the last year, powering millions of lab tests across all the US.
Location: Remote EST ONLY

sections.title: Why we need you
paras: Junction sits at the center of labs, providers, and the developers building on top of us. We process 20M lab tests today and are on track for 60M next year, and every 300th outpatient test in the US already runs through our systems. The product decisions we make now will shape how we get there.

This role owns how every order on Junction turns into a sample at the lab, one of the most sensitive and error prone moments in laboratory testing. When a sample isn't collected, or isn't collected properly, the patient never gets their result. That is the leading cause of missing results in lab testing today. Between the order and the lab, a patient has to find a collection option, and show up. That might be at a patient service center, with a mobile phlebotomist at their home, or with a self collection kit through the mail. The sample then has to be collected correctly and reach the right lab within its stability window, often through partners we don't directly control. This is one of the few product roles where the product only works if something happens in the physical world.

Solving this is the biggest opportunity in lab testing, and it starts with the patient. A patient-centric experience is how we get more people lab results and get better care delivered faster, in more places, more reliably. That is becoming Junction's most differentiated value proposition, and this role will own it. You'll expand where and how patients can get tested, including in their own homes. You'll improve the experience so more people follow through and get collected correctly the first time. You'll also build the national network of collection sites, phlebotomists and couriers behind it, and keep it reliable as volume grows.

sections.title: What you'll be doing day to day
bullets: Get more orders to a sample at the lab: from scheduling and reminders to where collection is available, you'll own the levers that get patients to follow through.
Own the physical path: kits and supplies, transport and routing each sample to the right lab, built alongside our Lab Operations team.
Expand where patients can get tested: launch new collection partners, including mobile phlebotomy and at-home kits, and decide where coverage and experience matters most.
Make calls with incomplete information: and flag the ones that need a wider conversation. Don't leave your team waiting on you.
Turn real-world signal into roadmap: customer pain, production issues, vendor behavior, support escalations. You're the person who sees the pattern and does something with it.
Partner with Product Ops on launches: so GTM, Success, Support and Operations are ready when the product is.
Help build the product function: how we plan, how we write, how we talk to customers, how we measure success.

ashby:partly.com:f7009127-349d-4716-ada0.summary: Note: Partly is headquartered in Austin, TX with offices in London, UK, Christchurch, NZ and Auckland, NZ. Wherever you're based, we'll connect you with your nearest office for onboarding, and fly you to join the full team for our quarterly "Season Openers" (we cover travel and accommodation). If you're relocating to join us, we can also assist with relocation costs.

sections.title: 🚀 Our Story
paras: Partly is building the infrastructure for anyone to repair anything. We believe everything built should be repairable, and we're building frontier AI to put repair knowledge to work, starting with the $2tn automotive market.

Our model, Interpreter, is the first AI purpose-built to understand repair. Trained on 1M+ car models and 1B+ parts, it reads a repair job the way an estimator does, resolves damage into the exact purchasable part, and shows its reasoning with a confidence score. On real production jobs, an estimator working with Interpreter reaches 98.8% parts-list accuracy, against 92.1% with today's tools. It powers PartlyRepair, used by collision shops, workshops and suppliers to take the admin off the job; PartlyLabs, the agentic infrastructure enterprises use to deploy Interpreter across their own workflows; and a developer API.

Founded by ex-Rocket Lab engineers, we've raised a $50m Series B led by DST Global (Anthropic, Airbnb, Meta, TikTok, Spotify), with Blackbird Ventures, WNDR, Activant Capital, Icehouse Ventures, Square Peg, Airtree and Ecliptic Venture Capital. Hear it from the team: Why Partly exists and AI at Partly .

sections.title: 🖍️ This role
paras: Insurers and work providers pay for the repair and set the rules it runs by. This role owns Partly's entire product relationship with them.

Partly creates value for insurers through three layers, and you own how all three land for this customer. Interpreter , our domain-specific AI foundation model, turns damage and estimate data into an accurate, complete parts picture early in the claim. Rails , our API layer, lets insurers and the systems they already run integrate directly with Partly's job processing infrastructure. And our agentic, highly automated user-level capabilities progressively absorb work that is manual across the industry today. Together these move the metrics an insurer is measured on: total cost of risk, cycle times, customer satisfaction, total loss rate and operational efficiency across the claims organisation.

You build for several distinct personas inside the insurer's workflow, each needing a different product on the same foundation: appraisers reviewing parts decisions and authorising spend; claims handlers and adjusters running the file; dispute and escalation teams revisiting jobs long after they close; network managers allocating work; and the parts, procurement and sustainability leads who set policy in the first place. You are the single accountable person for the value insurers get from Partly, and for what that unlocks across the rest of the network.

sections.title: 💻 What you'll own
bullets: Verification and Audit. Automating the manual claim verification insurer engineers perform today, and extending it into the value band nobody currently checks. Key metrics: share of claims verified without manual review, verification turnaround, engineer hours displaced, value recovered per verified claim.

sections.title: Own your product, end-to-end
bullets: Define and evolve the product vision, strategy and roadmap for insurer products globally, aligned with company direction and the wider platform.
Continuously assess and improve Product-Market Fit across markets with materially different claims structures, parts policies and competitive incumbents.
Decide deliberately what is global and what is local, and defend that line when a single account pushes on it.
Own key product, growth and commercial metrics and use them to steer every decision.
Act as the single accountable owner, for successes, failures and everything in between.

Through PHIL's digital stakeholder experiences, patient access services, market access solutions, and distribution models, pharma manufacturers can deliver affordable and timely therapy access to patients, resulting in more patients staying on their treatment plans longer. Consequently, pharma manufacturers are enabled for more innovation and more patients are able to access the therapy they need.

The team at PHIL is a group of like-minded individuals from varying backgrounds, passionate about creating a new and innovative healthcare platform that is focused on patient experience and overall human wellbeing. Strong organizational and prioritization skills, capable of owning 15 to 20 onboarding projects simultaneously.
Proven ability to drive implementations forward efficiently: managing complexity, following up consistently, maintaining momentum, and achieving successful outcomes within tight timelines.
A product-curious mindset, comfortable with products that are still evolving, and able to learn new systems quickly and shape workflows that maximize user value.

SAM s will be responsible for product performance at a territory level and expected to be a disease category expert and product champion. The SAM will provide account management support and exhibit business knowledge of the local landscape to assess key stakeholders plus future trends within the marketplace.

sections.title: Job Responsibilities and Duties include, but are not limited to, the following:

Assume full ownership of assigned territory’s performance as a specialty account manager, building awareness for SYMBRAVO amongst key customers in a competitive therapeutic environment
Develop a comprehensive and effective territory business plan aimed at achieving and exceeding quarterly and annual goals established by commercial leadership
Promote within our approved labeling in a comprehensive, fair, and ethical manner that is consistent with industry specific and corporate legal and regulatory guidelines
Develop strong customer relationships by better understanding the customer’s needs
Serve as a resource/consultant to customers and staff regarding payer policies and processes (i.e., eligibility and benefit verification, prior-authorization, and appeals/denials)

sections.title: Qualifications / Requirements
bullets: Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university

Minimum of 5 years of field customer experience and/or account management. Minimum of 3 years Healthcare Professional experience with relevant CNS experience will also meet the qualifications for this role
5 years of consistent top performance in the pharmaceutical, biotech or medical sales space
Migraine/CNS experience strongly preferred
Demonstrated experience delivering outstanding results
Launch experience strongly preferred

greenhouse:braze:8089828.summary:
At Braze, we have found our people. We’re a genuinely approachable, exceptionally kind, and intensely passionate crew.

We seek to ignite that passion by setting high standards, championing teamwork, and creating work-life harmony as we collectively navigate rapid growth on a global scale while striving for greater equity and opportunity – inside and outside our organization.

To flourish here, you must be prepared to set a high bar for yourself and those around you. There is always a way to contribute: Acting with autonomy, having accountability and being open to new perspectives are essential to our continued success.

sections.title: WHAT YOU'LL DO
bullets: The field narrative: Take the core messaging and positioning built by the PMM team and shape it into a compelling, coherent story the field can carry into every conversation — by persona, segment, and stage of the funnel

The playbook, and how product information reaches the field: You own the system by which our products become legible to the GTM org: the plays, narratives, assets, and channels that ensure every seller knows what we offer, who it's for, why it matters now, and how to win against the alternatives

Braze Services Marketing: Own the GTM narrative for our in-house services — support, onboarding, and education — and articulate the distinct value of Braze-delivered services to our customers as a meaningful differentiator
A small, agile, growing team: Lead and develop a team of GTM PMMs, setting priorities, raising the bar on craft, and building the foundation for a function that will scale globally over time

Partner with field leadership every day. Work hand-in-hand with Sales, Solutions Consultants, and CS leaders to understand where deals stall, what reps need, and how to translate product value into language that moves opportunities forward
Translate complex technology into the language of our buyers — and coach the field to do the same: You make hard things simple without making them shallow

Use AI as a force multiplier — judiciously: You're AI-literate and fluent in how AI is reshaping both martech and the practice of marketing. You know when AI meaningfully accelerates the work and when human judgment has to lead
Prioritize ruthlessly: Focus your team's energy on the narratives, launches, and plays that move the needle for the business — and have the judgment and the spine to say no to the rest

sections.title: How Success Is Measured
paras: You can measure and report on your work, and you hold yourself accountable to business outcomes — not activity. Success in this role is measured against pipeline, product adoption, pipeline progression, and overall program impact, and you'll be expected to show that connection clearly and consistently.

sections.title: WHO YOU ARE
bullets: A marketer who loves working with Sales and Customer Success. You're energized by the field, not protective of distance from it. The field trusts you as a subject-matter expert; Marketing trusts you as a strategic, thoughtful partner
A messaging craftsperson. You can take a positioning doc and a complex product and turn it into something sharp, memorable, and sales-ready. Strong messaging chops are non-negotiable
Fluent in the sales motion. You understand how deals actually get done and build for the way the field really sells
Deeply curious. You ask why. You dig into the product, the market, the competition, and the customer until you understand them well enough to make them simple
An exceptional writer and presenter. You write with clarity and edge, and you can command a room — a sales kickoff stage, an exec readout, or a field enablement session
Steeped in martech. You bring deep experience in the martech space, including a strong grasp of AI innovations and the competitive landscape
A sharp prioritizer and a builder of trust across cross-functional teams
10+ years of experience in Product Marketing, GTM/field marketing, or a closely related GTM function, including experience leading and developing people

sections.title: THE DETAILS
bullets: Reports to: VP of Product Marketing
Location: Hybrid; must be based in one of our hub cities — New York (HQ), San Francisco, Chicago, or Austin
Travel: Up to 30%

greenhouse:catapultsports:8257897.summary:
Catapult is building the future of sports performance technology, with a mission to Unleash the Potential of every athlete and team on earth. Since 2006, our solutions have been leading the way in sports performance software, science, and data, in a world where 1% can literally mean the difference between winning and losing.

sections.title: WE EXIST TO IMPROVE THE PERFORMANCE OF ATHLETES AND TEAMS

greenhouse:coinbase:8234060.summary: Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase , we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” Learn more about working at Coinbase .

sections.title: Team/ Role Paragraph:
paras: FinHub owns how money moves at Coinbase. Every dollar and token that enters, leaves, or moves within the company runs through this platform - fiat across ACH, wires, cards, RTP, and SEPA, crypto across dozens of blockchain networks, and internal movement across ledgers, legal entities, and customer accounts. As a Group Product Manager on the FinHub team within Platform , you'll own the systems that ensure every fund flow reaches a correct terminal state - the controls that stop unsafe movement, the detection that catches what slips through, and the remediation that recovers it. You'll set the reliability standard for money movement at Coinbase and lead through influence to hold the company to it.

sections.title: What you’ll do:
bullets: Own the multi-year vision and strategy for money movement reliability and controls across fiat and crypto, defining per-rail service levels and resolution targets for every fund flow.

Build the controls infrastructure governing money movement - determining which risk, compliance, and financial controls apply to each flow, verifying they ran, and confirming they passed before funds move.
Drive real-time detection and end-to-end tracing across payment rails, blockchain networks, controls, and the ledger to identify and resolve failures fast.
Scale correctness through AI agents that propose controls from product specs, triage alerts before an engineer opens them, and remediate within governed limits.
Partner with Compliance, Risk, Finance, and every product group that moves money to establish control ownership and hold teams accountable for their fund flows.

Track record owning strategy for large-scale money movement or financial systems - payment processing, transfers, ledgers, reconciliation, or the reliability layers around them.
Deep technical fluency in distributed systems, event streaming, idempotency, double-entry ledgering, reconciliation, and the design of preventive and detective controls.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: AI is changing how data practitioners write, debug, and ship dbt code. As Staff Product Manager for Developer Experience , you will set the strategy for how that change plays out in dbt.

Imagine Pediatrics is a tech enabled, pediatrician led medical group reimagining care for children with special health care needs. We deliver 24/7 virtual first and in home medical, behavioral, and social care, working alongside families, providers, and health plans to break down barriers to quality care. We do not replace existing care teams; we enhance them, providing an extra layer of support with compassion, creativity, and an unwavering commitment to children with medical complexity.

Families come to Imagine Pediatrics with real needs: a medication refill, a piece of medical equipment, a benefits application, follow-up after a hospital stay. As a Staff Product Manager, you’ll own the systems that make sure each of those needs is captured, has a clear owner on our care team, and actually gets delivered on. This is how we turn our care model into meaningful value for families.

sections.title: From the job description
paras: AI is central to how we’ll do this at scale. You’ll decide where AI and automation can take coordination work off our care teams so they spend their time on families instead of tracking, routing and chasing work, and you’ll prove it with measured results.

Our care model blends virtual and in-home care for children with special health care needs and their families. The product you own is where care teams see what families need, pick up the work and finish it, every day.

Product area: How family needs are captured, assigned, tracked and resolved across our care teams. That includes the shared view of patients and work care teams use every day; tasking and handoffs between roles; messaging with families by chat, text and email; internal care team communication; and follow-up after hospital discharges.
AI and automation in care coordination to:
bullets: capture needs from family conversations and messages
route and assign work to the right person
prioritize what’s most urgent
summarize a need’s history for whoever picks it up next
flag needs that are stalling before a family feels it
Primary users: Navigators, nurses, resource specialists, pharmacists and other care team members coordinating care. Families are users too, through the messages and updates they receive.

North star: % of family needs resolved within target time. You’ll also track how quickly each need gets a named owner, how many needs stall without progress, and how much care team time goes to coordination overhead rather than to families.

First-year outcomes:


• Every family need has a named owner and a visible status, and care teams stop working across fragmented tools.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: We are seeking a Product Manager to own Tailscale's networking features — the layer that decides how traffic finds its destination by name on top of Tailscale’s seamless mesh connectivity solution. Concretely, you will own four feature sets: App Connectors , DNS , Funnel , and Tailscale Serve & Services .

A tailnet gives every device an identity and an address. Networking features are what turn addresses into something a person, a script, or an AI agent can actually use — a name, a service, an app, a URL.

This is the most user-visible role in Tailscale's Dataplane Platform, and the work is as much product design as it is networking. DNS settings, connector topologies, and service definitions are configured by network engineers and IT admins in the admin console, API, and CLI, and the distance between "magical" and "unusable" is the object model, the defaults, and the error messages.
bullets: App Connectors route traffic to specific SaaS and private applications by name, so access follows the app rather than the IP.
DNS — MagicDNS, split DNS, custom name servers, search domains

Tailscale Serve & Services make a workload — not a machine — the unit of connectivity and access: addressable, load-balanced, and durable across the instances behind it. This is the wedge that lets customers replace a service registry, and eventually much of what they use a service mesh for, with Tailscale.
Funnel is Tailscale's ingress story: securely exposing a Service running inside the tailnet to the public internet, from a hobbyist sharing a dev server to production webhooks and public endpoints.

sections.title: Key Responsibilities
bullets: Own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for Tailscale's networking features: App Connectors, DNS, Funnel, and Tailscale Services

greenhouse:wunderkind:8330857.summary:
Wunderkind ads are 'behaviorally triggered', meaning that ads are served on a premium list of publishers only when a user is done consuming content. Our proprietary tag is integrated directly on the publisher page to track on-site user behavior - making ' net new' ad placements. How we serve the ad is why we are different from our competitors in-market.

Rather than placing an ad in front of someone while they're actively trying to read content, our technology patiently waits until a visitor has stopped reading before rendering our ad on the page. And that patience pays off -- it turns out that when an ad experience respects the user's reason for visiting a page, the user respects the ad experience in return. This unique, brand safe approach to ad experience gives an advertiser's message more attention and greater engagement.

smartrecruiters:mattelinc:74400015045821.summary: Mattel Digital Studios (MDS) is a cross-functional division that leverages digital innovation to amplify Mattel’s iconic brands, expanding into digital gaming, interactive experiences, and emerging technologies. Working across multiple products and partners, the team focuses on unlocking the value of AI, data, and modern development frameworks to power personalization, content creation, and next-generation play experiences.

sections.title: The Opportunity:
paras: As part of this ecosystem, the Applied AI function sits at the intersection of product innovation and technical execution—unlocking new capabilities across creative workflows, internal tooling, and development pipelines.

sections.title: What Your Impact Will Be:
paras: As a Senior Technical Product Manager, Applied AI, you will define, build, and scale AI-powered tools, workflows, and decision-support systems across Mattel Digital Studios. You will be accountable for identifying friction in cross-functional workflows — process misalignment, communication overhead, unreliable data, and stretched team bandwidth — and for translating that friction into a prioritized portfolio of AI solutions that measurably move the business.

You will manage a portfolio framed in three buckets — Quick Wins, Efficiency Gains, and Strategic Bets — with the strongest opportunities progressing from proof-of-concept into strategic pilot and broader MDS rollout. The scope spans workflow automation, internal tooling, creative and content-generation tools, and decision-support systems tied to real operational use cases.

Unlike traditional product roles, this position requires hands-on technical execution. You will actively build prototypes, experiment with AI models and APIs, and develop working solutions; but success goes beyond prototyping — it is seeing opportunities through productization, rollout, stakeholder alignment, team enablement, and repeatability across disciplines. You will partner with MDS leadership and the Product, Engineering, Operations, and Creative teams, bringing external vendors where buying beats building.

sections.title: Portfolio & Pain-Point Ownership
bullets: Own the applied AI roadmap from pitch to production — with direction and buy-in from MDS leadership, balancing speed, experimentation, and long-term value creation.
Identify and surface use cases and friction—assessing feasibility and scalability, translating them into high-impact AI opportunities.
Manage the opportunity portfolio—graduating the strongest proofs-of-concept into strategic pilots and broader MDS rollout.
Translate business needs into AI-powered tools, workflow automations, and decision-support solutions, defining clear requirements, success metrics, adoption targets, and iteration plans

sections.title: Experiment, Innovate & Build
bullets: Continuously explore emerging AI capabilities and evaluate their application for internal tools, workflows, and content pipelines; apply them where operational impact, not novelty, justifies the work.

Build prototypes, lightweight applications, automations, and decision-support tools. Work hands-on, using modern AI platforms — LLM APIs, multimodal models, agent frameworks, orchestration tools, and evaluation harnesses.
Rapidly test and iterate on new ideas with a focus on measurable operational impact.
Partner with engineering, platform, and external vendors to productize, harden, and scale successful prototypes—owning build-vs-buy judgment and seeing opportunities through to live deployment.

smartrecruiters:sgs:744000162082529.summary: Act as a liaison or contact between clients, laboratory management and department personnel. Also responsible for providing resolution to client service issues and technical support to laboratory personnel and clients.

sections.title: JOB FUNCTIONS
bullets: Provide quality and timely response to internal and external client inquiries and requests
Communicate results problems and discrepancies to clients and follow issue through to a satisfactory conclusion
Track and trend client data as required
Identify client concerns, complaints, and trends and recommend changes to accommodate client needs
Set up new client accounts in LIMS and create required documents for sample submission for new clients
Maintain records of all client communications and requirements
Notify laboratory of special client requirements and monitor for compliance
Ensure compliance to ISO 17025 standards are maintained

sections.title: EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE
bullets: 4-year degree in Food Science, Microbiology or closely related field; Alternatively, equivalent work experience Preferred
High school Diploma or GED Required
Effective problem prevention and problem-solving skills Required
Written and verbal communication skills necessary to cross multiple disciplines Required
Proficiency with Microsoft Word and Excel Required
Proficiency with LIMS and Client Portal systems Required
Ability to interact with clients, affiliates, and employees effectively while maintaining a professional and pleasant work approach even under stressful conditions Required
1+ years of laboratory experience Required
